LESSON: GRAMMAR 11.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERNS: INTERROGATIVES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar 11.3.1 Language Patterns: Interrogatives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar 11.3.1 Language Patterns: Interrogatives, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we ask questions? 2. Which words do we use to ask questions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar 11.3.1 Language Patterns: Interrogatives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: learners develop relationships as they use appropriate interrogatives to ask questions.

● Digital literacy: learners develop the skill of interacting with technology as they interact with digital devices when searching for information

online.

Values:
Responsibility: accountability as learners choose the correct content to watch when directed to view videos, cartoons or pictures.

Link to other subjects:

Learner is able to link the concept of interrogatives to their learning in Kiswahili.
